entries.reason: Single Responsibility — The draft is focused on one concern: introducing task-scoped flow foundations for T2.; Unambiguous Requirements — Some requirements use non-verifiable phrasing like “最小配線” and scope boundaries without measurable acceptance criteria.; Complete Context — Many requirement bullets specify actions but do not consistently pair explicit trigger conditions with expected “shall” behavior.; No Hardcoded Secrets — No credentials or secret literals are present; this is a requirements draft, not secret-bearing source code.; Prioritize Requirements — The draft lists many requirements but does not define an explicit priority order among them.; Impact on Existing Features — It has a dedicated impact section, including explicit breaking-change and non-impact statements.; Present Recommendations with Reasoning — Recommendations are provided, but the basis (docs/, guardrails, or code patterns) is not explicitly cited per question.; Explore Before Asking — The Q&A shows user questions/choices but does not evidence prior docs/code exploration before asking.; Proactively Raise Related Implications — It proactively covers migration implications, future parallel-task implications, and downstream task boundaries.; Confirm Brainstorm vs. Decision Before Critiquing — The draft records decisions, but no explicit brainstorming-vs-decision confirmation before critique is shown.; Capture Digressions in draft.md — Digressions and decision trails are captured in the draft’s Q&A and alternatives sections.; Draft Stays at Requirements Level — It includes implementation-level detail (method names, step sequences, load-time throw behavior, commit order).; Backward — Compatible CLI Interface — Existing command semantics are stated as preserved, so no migration plan is required for CLI changes.

Single Responsibility — Draft focuses on one concern: introducing the flow/task state-management foundation for spec 196 (T2).; Unambiguous Requirements — Some requirements use non-verifiable wording (e.g., “実装進行を妨げない”), leaving acceptance criteria ambiguous.; Complete Context — Requirements consistently pair trigger conditions (`When`) with expected behavior (`shall`).; No Hardcoded Secrets — Content is a requirements draft and includes no source code secrets or embedded credentials.; Prioritize Requirements — Requirements are explicitly prioritized (P1–P4) and marked as ordered.; Impact on Existing Features — A dedicated impact section lists breaking and non-breaking effects on existing behavior.; Present Recommendations with Reasoning — Each Q&A item includes an AI recommendation and cites its basis (docs, guardrails, or code patterns).; Explore Before Asking — Draft explicitly states pre-investigation of issue/cac6/code before running Q&A.; Proactively Raise Related Implications — It proactively covers migration implications, active-flow risks, and future extension impacts.; Confirm Brainstorm vs. Decision Before Critiquing — Q2 explicitly records confirmation of brainstorming vs decision state before critique.; Capture Digressions in draft.md — Digressive discussion points and outcomes are captured in the draft’s Q&A section.; Draft Stays at Requirements Level — Content remains at requirement/scope level without function-level design or implementation steps.; Backward — Compatible CLI Interface — Existing CLI behavior is stated as unchanged; migration guidance is still included for state-schema breaking changes.

Single Responsibility — The spec stays focused on T2 state-management changes (schema, store/manager/helpers, and related tests) and defers unrelated CLI/gate/run rewiring.; Unambiguous Requirements — Most requirements are written as verifiable `When ... shall ...` behaviors with concrete fields, methods, and expected outcomes.; Complete Context — Several requirements (for example REQ-12 and REQ-15〜REQ-17) lack an explicit trigger condition paired with the expected behavior.; No Hardcoded Secrets — No API keys, passwords, tokens, or other secret literals are present in the specification content.; No Silent Error Swallowing — The spec does not prescribe empty catches or silent error discard patterns; it explicitly requires throws in failure cases.; Prioritize Requirements — There are 20 requirements but no priority ordering (such as P0/P1/P2 or ordered criticality) is defined.; Impact on Existing Features — Existing-feature impact is explicitly addressed, including preserved external CLI behavior and noted internal scope-inference changes.; Bounded Resource Usage — The described changes do not introduce recursive/retry/bulk-loading loops that require explicit bounds.; Changes Require Test Coverage — New behavior is paired with concrete unit-test additions and explicit pass criteria (`npm test`).; Spec Includes Test Strategy — A dedicated Test Strategy section defines what to test, how to test, and fixture/update policy.; Synthesize Draft, Do Not Copy — No separate draft content is provided here, so this check is inapplicable to the submitted text.; Record Unresolved Points as Open Questions — Unresolved items are explicitly handled via an Open Questions section, which currently states none.; Include 'Why This Approach' Rationale — The spec includes a dedicated rationale section with explicit design-choice justifications.; Backward — Compatible CLI Interface — CLI command/option semantics are stated as unchanged, and a migration plan is included for internal breaking data-format changes.; Exit Code Contract — The spec does not explicitly state non-zero exit-code behavior for failure paths in affected commands.
